title: Completion of a lattice monoid as supported formal series
statement: Let $r\geq0$, let $M\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$ be an additive subgroup, and put $Q=M\cap\mathbf N^r$, viewed as an additive monoid. Assume $Q$ is finitely generated. Let $L$ be a commutative local ring with finitely generated maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and assume that the canonical map $L\to\varprojlim_a L/\mathfrak m^a$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Write $L[Q]$ for the ring of finite sums $\sum_q c_qz^q$, with $z^qz^{q\prime}=z^{q+q\prime}$, and put $J=\mathfrak m L[Q]+(z^q:q\in Q\setminus\{0\})$. Let $T=\varprojlim_a L[Q]/J^a$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $A=L[[X_1,\ldots,X_r]]$ the formal power-series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The homomorphism $L[Q]\to A$, $z^q\mapsto X^q$, extends uniquely to an injective continuous $L$-algebra homomorphism $\iota:T\to A$, where $A$ has the $(\mathfrak m A+(X_1,\ldots,X_r))$-adic topology. Its image is exactly $A_Q=\{\sum_e c_eX^e:c_e=0\text{ for }e\notin Q\}$. The coefficient projection $\pi:A\to A_Q$, $\sum_e c_eX^e\mapsto\sum_{e\in Q}c_eX^e$, is additive, fixes $A_Q$ pointwise, and satisfies $\pi(ab)=a\pi(b)$ for every $a\in A_Q$ and $b\in A$. Thus $\rho=\iota^{-1}\pi:A\to T$ is a $T$-linear map with $\rho\iota=\operatorname{id}_T$.

proof.text: Put $B=L[Q]$, $I=\mathfrak mA+(X_1,\ldots,X_r)A$ and let $j:B\to A$ be the monomial map. Since $Q$ is finitely generated by hypothesis, choose finitely many nonzero generators of $Q$, using the empty list when $Q=\{0\}$. Apply [lem-trf-monoid-degree-filtration-truncations] with $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak m$: it supplies an injective algebra map $j$ and $D\geq1$ with $J^n\subseteq j^{-1}(I^n)$ and $j^{-1}(I^{Dn})\subseteq J^n$. In particular $j(J)\subseteq I$ and the two filtrations are cofinal (take $N=Dn\geq n$).

proof.text: The assumed bijection from $L$ to its completion and the bounds from step 1 verify all hypotheses of [lem-trf-monoid-completion-coefficient-embedding]. Its coefficient-limit construction gives the unique continuous injective $L$-algebra extension $\iota:T\to A$, with $\iota x-jf_n\in I^n$ for any representatives of $x$, and with every coefficient outside $Q$ zero. Hence $\iota(T)\subseteq A_Q$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70 gives completed monoid models only; auxiliary agent algebra, extracting old proof steps 3--5, step 6 first sentence, and step 7 of lem-trf-completed-monoid-support-projection, with the filtration bounds expressed as hypotheses.

proof.text: For $F\in A_Q$, [lem-trf-monoid-degree-filtration-truncations] gives $b_n(F)=\sum_{q\in Q,\ |q|<Dn}c_q(F)z^q$ and the compatible family $x_n=b_n(F)\bmod J^n$. Fix $e$ and $k\geq1$, and take $n\geq k+|e|$. Since $D\geq1$, the truncation has the exact $e$-coefficient of $F$. The coefficient congruence of [lem-trf-monoid-completion-coefficient-embedding] gives $c_e(\iota x)\equiv c_e(F)\pmod{\mathfrak m^k}$. Equality for every $k$ implies equality in $L$ by injectivity of its completion map [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Thus $\iota x=F$, proving $\iota(T)=A_Q$.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-lattice-support-coefficient-retraction], applied to the given subgroup $M$ and coefficient ring $L$, $A_Q$ is a subalgebra and its coefficient projection $\pi$ is additive, fixes $A_Q$, and satisfies $\pi(ab)=a\pi(b)$ for $a\in A_Q$. Steps 2--3 give an injective $L$-algebra map $\iota:T\to A$ with image exactly $A_Q$. Apply the transported-retraction clause of the same lemma with $R=T$ and $\varphi=\iota$. It yields $\rho=\iota^{-1}\pi$, with $\rho(\iota(t)b)=t\rho(b)$ and $\rho\iota=\operatorname{id}_T$, which proves all remaining claims.
